html:
The General Maritime Treaty was signed in early 1820 between Britain and the sheikhs of the coast that is now the UAE, after a British fleet from Bombay had burned the ships and fort of Ras al-Khaimah in late 1819.

Britain called the Al Qasimi of Ras al-Khaimah pirates who attacked ships of the East India Company. A later ruler of Sharjah has argued that the charge was largely a pretext for control of the Gulf trade. The sheikhs agreed to stop raiding at sea.

A permanent truce followed in 1853, and the coast became known as the Trucial Coast (Trucial States). In 1892 the sheikhs gave Britain control of their foreign affairs. The system lasted until the founding of the UAE in 1971.
